ticket.title: outfeed gate contracts step fails when the member index does not exist yet
ticket.description:
outfeed gate -d miter passed fmt, clippy, tests and docs, then failed at contracts with no index at miter/.miter/miter.redb: run miter index first. A Tier 3 gate that needs a manually pre-built index is not runnable from a clean checkout, which is exactly the situation a gate exists for. The step should build the index itself, index into a temporary database, or treat a missing index as a warned skip.

REPRODUCED 2026-11-12, and it is worse than filed: it blocks verifying any ticket whose scope is a member repository. `storypole verify CO-3 --dir common` failed with the chain output:
  miter: no index at .../common/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb: run `miter index <PATH> --db ...` first
so the contracts step refuses from a clean checkout, exactly as this ticket says. The workaround is to build that index by hand first, after which the same verify passes (CO-3 verified exit 0) - which is the point: a Tier 3 gate that needs a manually prepared artefact is not runnable where a gate matters. Note the failure surfaced through GB-341-style chain reporting, so the operator sees the reason rather than a bare exit code.

FIXED 2026-11-12 (outfeed 845412c), verified on the outfeed chain (exit 0) - whose contracts step is the thing that was broken, so the receipt is the end-to-end proof.

The step now indexes into a temporary database and checks against it: nothing is written into the repository, and an index left over from an earlier run cannot decide a result. Fixing that exposed a second defect the old failure had been hiding: a member checking without the suite contracts allowlist reported the suite own non-mirror declarations as drift - role_override_config.api_key, a secret deliberately absent from TypeScript - so a clean benchwork failed while the suite root was clean. The step now passes the allowlist that governs it: the suite when this is a member, its own otherwise.

PROVEN from a repository with no index at all: `outfeed gate benchwork --skip fmt --skip clippy --skip tests --skip lockfiles --skip docs` reports 1 passed, 0 failed. Before the fix the same command refused with `miter: no index at .../benchwork/.gaugeblock/miter/miter.redb`.

An honest note on the route: the first attempt passed the repository as the index source while also making it the working directory, which doubled a relative root into repo/repo and surfaced as an ingestion i/o error that read like a missing index. The fix is a literal "." and a comment saying why.
